title: A clinical call to action – How developmental translational neuroscience can catalyze adolescent substance use treatment: The example of ADAPT
title_zh: 临床行动号召——发展转化神经科学如何催化青少年物质使用治疗：ADAPT（Adolescent Developmentally-Appropriate health Promotion Therapy）的示例
abstract: As the field more actively recognizes the unique facets of adolescent neural, social, and behavioral development, it is clear that adult models of addiction are incongruent with the nature of the developing brain, adolescent substance use behavior, and behavioral outcomes in substance use treatment with adolescents. The present review highlights how developmental translational neuroscience can address this gap by informing and guiding the creation and implementation of more effective, neurodevelopmentally-targeted treatment programming for adolescents. This is illustrated with the example of Adolescent Developmentally-Appropriate health Promotion Therapy (ADAPT), a novel substance use treatment grounded in developmental translational (integrated human brain and behavioral) empirical research. Ultimately, this review aims to provide clinicians working in direct care settings with adolescents engaged in substance use a contemporary perspective on how and why developmental translational neuroscience is relevant to the clinical context, as well as a concrete example of how developmental translational neuroscience can inform substance use treatment for this high need and underserved age group.
abstract_zh: 随着该领域更积极地认识到青少年神经、社会和行为发展的独特方面，显而易见，成人成瘾模型与发育中大脑、青少年物质使用行为以及青少年物质使用治疗的行为结果不相符。本综述强调发展转化神经科学如何通过为青少年制定和实施更有效、针对神经发育的治疗方案提供信息和指导，从而填补这一空白。以青少年发展适宜健康促进疗法（ADAPT）为例，ADAPT是一种基于发展转化（整合人类大脑与行为）实证研究的新型物质使用治疗。最终，本综述旨在为直接护理环境中与青少年物质使用相关的临床医生提供关于发展转化神经科学在临床背景中的相关性及其为何重要的当代视角，并提供一个具体示例，说明发展转化神经科学如何为这一高需求且服务不足的年龄群体的物质使用治疗提供信息。
